```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

This vignette works through the illustrative example of a methods review of
indirect calorimetry and 13C tracing (Tremblay, in preparation), with the
default constants of oxidizr. The values describe one subject exercising at
about 60% of maximal O2 uptake while ingesting glucose from maize; they are
not data from a study.

```{r setup, message = FALSE}
library(oxidizr)

vo2 <- 2.80; vco2 <- 2.52        # L/min, STPD
d_exp <- -20.5; d_ref <- -24.5    # breath delta 13C (per mil PDB), glucose and control trials
d_ing <- -11.0; d_glu <- -13.0    # ingested glucose and plasma glucose
```

## Constants

The defaults are dioleoyl-palmitoyl-glycerol as the reference fat, Kleiber's
standard protein without sulfur, a molar volume of 22.414 L/mol and the energy
values of the Institute of Medicine (2005). See `vignette("stoichiometry")`.

```{r}
k <- oxidation_constants()
k
```

## Total carbohydrate and fat oxidation

```{r}
ox <- calc_substrate_oxidation(
  CalorimetryData(data = data.frame(id = 1, time = 60, vo2 = vo2, vco2 = vco2))
)
ox[, c("cho_total", "fat_total", "rer")]
```

## Exogenous, plasma, liver and muscle glucose

The fraction of expired CO2 that comes from a labeled substrate is
(delta_exp - delta_ref) / (delta_substrate - delta_ref). Dividing the CO2 it
represents by `k$co2_cho_ratio` (L CO2 per g glucose) gives grams of glucose.

```{r}
exo <- vco2 * (d_exp - d_ref) / (d_ing - d_ref) / k$co2_cho_ratio
pla <- vco2 * (d_exp - d_ref) / (d_glu - d_ref) / k$co2_cho_ratio
round(c(
  total_cho  = ox$cho_total,
  fat        = ox$fat_total,
  exogenous  = exo,
  plasma     = pla,
  liver      = pla - exo,
  muscle     = ox$cho_total - pla
), 2)
```

In a study, `calc_exogenous_cho()`, `calc_plasma_cho()` and
`calc_cho_partition()` do these steps for every subject and time point, with
the reference taken from the control trial (`calc_rref()`).

## How much the constants matter

```{r}
lipids <- c("diop", "tag_type", "tripalmitin", "pos", "fatty_acid")
t(sapply(lipids, function(l) {
  kk <- oxidation_constants(lipid = l)
  c(cho = kk$cho_vco2 * vco2 + kk$cho_vo2 * vo2,
    fat = kk$fat_vo2 * vo2 + kk$fat_vco2 * vco2)
})) |> round(3)
```

## How much an error in RER matters

An error of +0.01 in RER (VCO2 = 2.548 instead of 2.52 L/min) changes
carbohydrate and fat oxidation by these percentages:

```{r}
err <- calc_substrate_oxidation(
  CalorimetryData(data = data.frame(id = 1, time = 60, vo2 = vo2, vco2 = vco2 + 0.01 * vo2))
)
round(100 * c(cho = err$cho_total / ox$cho_total - 1,
              fat = err$fat_total / ox$fat_total - 1), 1)
```

`vignette("uncertainty")` propagates measurement uncertainty through a whole
study.

## References

Institute of Medicine (2005). *Dietary Reference Intakes for Energy, Carbohydrate, Fiber, Fat, Fatty Acids, Cholesterol, Protein, and Amino Acids*. National Academies Press. https://doi.org/10.17226/10490
